title: Nut-Free Raspberry Cream Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vanilla cupcakes with a raspberry cream filling, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes use real raspberry puree for both the filling and the frosting, so the pink color comes from fruit, not dye. The base is a simple vanilla batter that stays soft for two days. I tested this recipe in my home kitchen with fresh and frozen raspberries, and both worked well. It is a safe pick for nut-free bake sales since every ingredient is easy to check on a label.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh or frozen raspberries, plus 1 cup for frosting
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Make the raspberry puree first. Simmer 2 cups raspberries with 2 tbsp sugar for 5 minutes, then strain out the seeds. Cool the puree fully before using it.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar in a large bowl for 2 minutes, until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each. Stir in vanilla.
Add the flour mix and milk in three additions, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until combined.
Fold in 3 tbsp of the cooled raspberry puree, leaving swirls in the batter.
Divide batter into liners, filling each about two thirds full. Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool completely.
Once cool, core out the center of each cupcake and fill with 1 tsp raspberry puree.
Beat butter for the frosting until smooth, then add powdered sugar in two batches.
Add 3 to 4 tbsp raspberry puree and the heavy cream, then beat 3 minutes until fluffy and pink. Pipe onto cupcakes and top with a fresh raspberry.
tips: Strain the puree well or your frosting will look speckled instead of smooth pink.
Chill the puree before adding it to frosting so the buttercream does not turn soupy.
If using frozen raspberries, thaw and drain extra liquid before simmering.
Core the cupcakes with a small knife or an apple corer for an even filling pocket.

faq.question: Can I use raspberry jam instead of fresh puree?
faq.answer: Yes, but strain the jam first to remove seeds and thin it with 1 tsp water. Fresh puree gives a brighter pink color and lighter flavor.

faq.question: Why is my frosting pink but streaky instead of even?
faq.answer: This happens when the puree is not fully mixed in. Beat the frosting 1 extra minute on medium speed to blend the color evenly.

faq.question: Are these cupcakes safe for a nut-free classroom bake sale?
faq.answer: Yes, every ingredient here is nut-free. Just check your specific butter and sugar brands for a shared facility warning.

faq.question: Can I make the filling and frosting a day ahead?
faq.answer: Yes. Store the puree in a sealed jar in the fridge for up to 3 days, then bring to room temperature before mixing into frosting.

conclusion: These raspberry cream cupcakes prove you do not need food coloring for a real pink frosting. Fresh fruit does all the work here, in both color and flavor.
